summary: Codex is tested through an **integration-heavy pyramid**: Sokrates' path-based test scope holds 499,465 LOC in 1,862 files (ratio 0.70 to 712,527 main LOC) and the script finds a further 140,692 LOC of inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules in 501 main files that Sokrates counts as main code - 47k of them in the TUI. The core engine's `tests/suite` (168k LOC, 116 modules) boots a real Codex against a `wiremock` model server; the app-server suite (118 modules) spawns the real binary and drives it over JSON-RPC; the TUI is snapshot-first with 683 `insta` files; the SDKs test against recorded-response proxies and optionally the real binary. Coverage is inferred from what tests reference, not measured: the core engine (ratio 2.16), app-server API (1.23), extensibility, code-mode, exec-server, auth and SDKs are well tested and all ten risk-synthesis hotspots have a direct test file; the protocol crate (0.08 path-based, 0.33 inline) and the sandboxing & policy component (0.26 + 0.25, platform-gated and self-skipping) are thin. Test quality is high where it counts - whole-object `pretty_assertions`, mocking only at the model boundary, real filesystem and SQLite - but two mechanisms weaken what a green run proves: **1,320 `skip_if_no_network!`/`skip_if_sandbox!` call sites** return early and report pass whenever Codex runs its own tests in a sandbox, and **nextest retries every test once** by default while four tests are parked as `TODO: flaky`. Two compaction regression tests are ignored because current behaviour is known-incorrect. There are no property-based or fuzz tests for the patch, shell and JSONL parsers, doc tests are disabled in 135 crates, and the one medium reliability finding (unobserved turn-task panic) has no test. Findings: 18, of which 2 medium, 6 low, 10 info.

findings.title: Five layers: inline unit, sibling *_tests.rs, in-process integration behind a wiremock model server, subprocess JSON-RPC end-to-end, insta snapshots - no property, fuzz or doc tests
findings.description: **Unit tests** live in two shapes: `#[cfg(test)]` modules inside 501 main files (140,692 LOC, invisible to Sokrates' path-based test scope) and sibling `*_tests.rs` files wired in with `#[path]`, which AGENTS.md now mandates for new modules. **Integration tests** are one binary per crate (`tests/all.rs` pulling `tests/suite/*`): `core/tests/suite` has 116 modules that build an in-process Codex through `TestCodexBuilder` against a `wiremock` mock of the `/v1/responses` API, so the whole turn loop, tool execution and sandbox run for real while only the model is faked. **End-to-end tests** are the `app-server/tests/suite/v2` modules (118 files) that spawn the real `codex` binary as a subprocess and drive it over JSON-RPC stdio or websocket, plus the TypeScript SDK's Jest suite, which spawns `codex-rs/target/debug/codex`, and the Python SDK's `test_real_app_server_integration.py` gated by `RUN_REAL_CODEX_TESTS=1`. **Snapshot tests** via `insta` hold 737 `.snap` files, 683 of them in `codex-rs/tui`, and 38 in `core/tests/suite/snapshots` freezing request shapes. **Terminal rendering** has its own layer: a VT100 backend (`tui/tests/test_backend.rs`) that renders the real widget tree and asserts on screen contents. Criterion benchmarks (`utils/image/benches`) and the Bazel `e2e-benchmarks` target (tagged `manual`) are the only performance-as-test shapes.

findings.title: just test wraps cargo nextest with a local profile; cargo test is forbidden; insta, Bazel, Jest, pytest and unittest cover the other tiers
findings.description: The sanctioned entry point is **`just test`** (in `codex-rs`), which runs `cargo nextest run --no-fail-fast` under `NEXTEST_PROFILE=local` with a raised `RUST_MIN_STACK`; AGENTS.md forbids calling `cargo test` directly and prescribes `just test -p <crate>` first, then the whole suite only when `common`, `core` or `protocol` changed. findings.title: nextest retries every test once by default; four tests are ignored as flaky with only TODO names; leak-detection races are documented rather than fixed
findings.description: `.config/nextest.toml` sets **`retries = 1`** in the default profile with the comment that one transient failure should not fail full-CI - a blanket retry that masks intermittent failures in every crate, with no per-test justification and no tracking. Tests known to be flaky are parked with owner TODOs instead of issues: `pending_input.rs` `injected_user_input_triggers_follow_up_request_with_deltas` (`TODO(aibrahim): flaky`), `review.rs` `review_start_exec_approval_item_id_matches_command_execution_item` (`TODO(owenlin0): flaky`), and two Windows-only `flaky on windows` ignores in `review.rs` and `code_mode.rs`. `test_app_server.rs` and `mcp_process.rs` document that child cleanup timing is nondeterministic and can trip nextest's `LEAK` detection, and `tool_parallelism.rs` calls itself a timing-based test. The harness itself retries spawning the binary on `ExecutableFileBusy`. The script's 60 `flaky_markers` are mostly the `request_max_retries = 0` config line and should not be read as 60 flaky tests. cicd-scan already notes the arm Linux Bazel target disabled as flaky.

findings.title: 381 sleeps in tests - sleep-then-assert-absence waits, 25 ms polling loops, 54 env mutations serialised with serial_test - but no real network on the default path
findings.description: The script finds **381 `sleep` sites** in test code, 608 wall-clock reads and 13 randomness uses. Two patterns dominate. **Poll-with-sleep loops** (`sqlite_state.rs` loops 100 times over `try_exists` with 25 ms sleeps; `wait_for_*` helpers in the app-server suite) are bounded and rarely flaky but add up. **Fixed sleep then assert nothing happened** - `plugin_list.rs` sleeps 100 ms and then asserts a remote request count of zero - is the shape that cannot be made reliable, only slow. Process environment is mutated in **54 places** despite AGENTS.md asking tests to avoid it; the mitigations are `#[serial(...)]` groups in 25 files and explicit comments where it is unavoidable (`client.rs` 3488). Real network is not on the default path: the 1,130 `network_in_tests` hits are URL string literals in config fixtures (`https://chatgpt.com`, `https://example.test`, `https://github.com`), and the only tests that reach the internet (`live_cli.rs`, the tmux resize smoke) are `#[ignore]`. findings.title: 1,320 skip-macro call sites turn integration tests green when run inside a sandbox; 74 attribute skips include two compaction tests ignored because current behaviour is known-incorrect

findings.title: core_test_support and app_test_support: a builder that boots a real Codex against wiremock, a test binary that impersonates codex/apply_patch/sandbox via arg0, and a subprocess JSON-RPC client
findings.description: **`core_test_support`** (`core/tests/common`, 14 modules) is the centre of gravity: `TestCodexBuilder` boots a real `Codex` in a temp `CODEX_HOME` bound to a `wiremock::MockServer`, with `build_with_auto_env()` (local or remote exec environment), `build_with_streaming_server()` and `build_with_websocket_server()` variants; `responses.rs` provides the SSE/websocket event builders (`ev_function_call`, `ev_apply_patch_custom_tool_call`, `sse_completed`, ...) and `ResponseMock` for asserting on captured requests; `lib.rs` holds the eight `skip_if_*` macros. A `#[ctor]` in `suite/mod.rs` makes the test binary answer as `codex`, `apply_patch` and `codex-linux-sandbox` depending on `arg0`, so tools that spawn helpers work without a separate build. **`app_test_support`** (`app-server/tests/common`, 15 modules) spawns the real binary and wraps every JSON-RPC method in a `send_*_request` method on `TestAppServer` (about 150 of them), with a websocket delay interposer, auth fixtures, analytics and models-cache servers and rollout fixtures. The **TUI** has `chatwidget/tests/helpers.rs` (`test_config`, `render_bottom_popup`) and a VT100 backend for terminal-level tests. **SDKs**: `responsesProxy.ts` records requests and replays SSE, `setupCodexHome.ts` builds a temp home; Python `app_server_harness.py` is a `ThreadingHTTPServer` fake. A separate `app-server-test-client` crate is a manual exploration client, not an automated suite. Mock servers beyond the model: `apps_test_server.rs`, `analytics_server.rs`, `rmcp-client` `test_stdio_server`/`test_streamable_http_server` binaries for MCP, and `exec-server/tests/common/relay.rs`.

findings.title: 737 insta snapshots reviewed through cargo insta, request-shape snapshots in the core suite, and app-server schema fixtures regenerated by an ignored test
findings.description: Three golden-file systems. **insta snapshots**: 737 `.snap` files, 683 under `codex-rs/tui` (126 in `tui/src/snapshots`, the rest beside their modules), 52 in `core`, one each in `cli/doctor` and `ext/skills`; AGENTS.md prescribes the review loop (`cargo insta pending-snapshots`, `show`, `accept -p codex-tui`) and asks that snapshot updates be reviewed as part of the PR "so UI impact is easy to review". The core suite uses 38 snapshots to freeze the **shape of model requests** after compaction and resume. **Schema fixtures**: `app-server-protocol` commits the generated TypeScript and JSON Schema; a normal test asserts the committed tree equals a fresh export, and the writer is an `#[ignore]`d test invoked by `just write-app-server-schema`, so the fixtures cannot silently drift. There is no snapshot pruning or unreferenced-snapshot check beyond what `cargo insta` offers. `scripts/mcp_conformance` keeps regression baselines (`regression-baseline-v1.json`) for the MCP compliance runner.

evidence.snippet: update the existing snapshot). Review and accept snapshot updates as part of the PR so UI impact

findings.title: The turn-task panic path reliability-scan flagged has no test: tasks/mod_tests.rs covers telemetry, abort_tasks.rs covers interrupts, nothing panics inside a spawned turn
findings.description: `reliability-scan/isolation/turn-task-panic-never-observed` (medium) says a panic inside the `tokio::spawn`ed turn task is never joined, leaving the client waiting. No test exercises it: `core/src/tasks/mod_tests.rs` asserts session telemetry metrics, `core/tests/suite/abort_tasks.rs` covers `interrupt_long_running_tool_emits_turn_aborted` and the persisted abort marker, and no suite test injects a panic into a tool handler or turn future. Other reliability paths **are** tested: the rollout writer's reopen-and-retry (`writer_state_retries_write_error_before_reporting_flush_success`), malformed rollout lines (`recorder_tests.rs` asserts `parse_errors == 1`), stream errors (`stream_error_allows_next_turn.rs`), quota and retry-after handling, guardian timeouts (`guardian_review.rs`). This gap is narrow, which keeps it `low`; it is the one medium reliability finding whose fix would ship without a failing test first.

evidence.note: the only sibling test file: telemetry, not failure
closest existing test: interrupt, not panic

findings.recommendation: Add a suite test that registers a tool handler which panics, runs a turn, and asserts the client receives a turn error within the timeout; write it before changing `tasks/mod.rs` so the reliability fix is regression-guarded.

findings.title: No property-based or fuzz tests for the parsers that read untrusted input: apply_patch, the shell tree-sitter parser, the reverse JSONL scanner, execpolicy
findings.description: The script reports **0 property tests and 0 fuzz targets**; no `proptest`, `quickcheck`, `arbitrary` or `cargo-fuzz` appears in any `Cargo.toml`. The code has several hand-written parsers fed by the model or by files on disk - `apply-patch/src/parser.rs` (`parse_patch`, model output), the tree-sitter Bash/PowerShell command parsing behind exec policy, `rollout/src/reverse_jsonl_scanner.rs` (session files, partially written), the Starlark execpolicy evaluator, and the JSON-RPC decoders - each tested with hand-picked cases such as `skips_records_over_the_configured_limit`. For a system whose sandbox decisions depend on parsing a command line correctly, example-based tests alone leave the edge space unexplored. This is a missing layer on a stable, well unit-tested surface, so `low`.
findings.recommendation: Add `proptest` round-trip and no-panic properties for `parse_patch`, the reverse JSONL scanner and the shell command parser, and a `cargo-fuzz` target for `parse_patch` run on a schedule (the repo already has scheduled workflows).

findings.title: Posture: an integration-heavy pyramid whose green run proves the engine and API behave against a faked model on the platform it ran on - but not that every test actually ran
findings.description: The pyramid is **top-heavy by design**: AGENTS.md prefers integration tests for agent changes, and the result is 168k LOC in `core/tests/suite` and 86k in `app-server/tests` versus 141k LOC of inline units spread over 501 files. A green `just test` proves that the turn loop, tools, hooks, MCP, plugins, compaction, resume and the JSON-RPC surface behave as specified against a faked OpenAI API on **this** platform, with real filesystem, SQLite and child processes; it does not prove sandbox behaviour when run inside a sandbox (the `skip_if_*` macros return early and report pass), does not prove anything on the other four platforms until post-merge (`cicd-scan/testing/pr-vs-postmerge-split`), and tolerates one retry per test. **Most trusted**: the core suite and app-server v2 suite - whole-object assertions on captured requests and events, real internals, shared builders. **Least trusted**: the TUI's 683 snapshots (correct only as far as reviewers read accepted diffs), the sandboxing tests (platform-gated, self-skipping, two disabled in CI), and any suite run from a sandboxed agent. Coverage inferred from references, not measured. The three highest-leverage changes: make the skip macros visible (`finding:testing-scan/test-quality/skipped-tests`), replace the blanket nextest retry with targeted overrides (`finding:testing-scan/test-quality/flakiness`), and put one real sandbox-escape test per OS into the PR-blocking matrix (`finding:testing-scan/coverage-map/thin-sandboxing-policy`).

evidence.snippet: For agent changes prefer integration tests over unit tests. Integration tests are under `core/suite` and use `test_codex` to set up a test instance of codex.

evidence.note: what a green run does not prove

attributes.pyramid: integration-heavy: core suite 168k LOC, app-server e2e 86k, inline units 141k, snapshots 737
